newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND, May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND, May 16.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Friday.
- The Fine Gael party is to propose a 1.5 billion Irish pound programme of tax reductions over five years as a central plank of its election programme.

- The government has made a pre-election allocation of 7.8 billion Irish pounds in National Lottery funds, telling government deputies first in order to allow them to claim credit in their constituencies.
- A former chief executive of national airline Aer Lingus has called for the company to be privatised.
- Around 35,000 new customers and a surge in demand of seven percent drove ESB's profits beyond expectations in 1996, to 151 million Irish pounds before exceptional costs.
- The first opinion poll of the Irish general election shows Fianna Fail support slipping by three points, but the party still on course to lead the next government.
- A former chief executive of private airline Ryanair has taken legal action against the company and one of its founders and largest shareholders Tony Ryan.
- General election battle to centre on taxation.
- Irish Life new business sales in the first four months of 1997 up 10 percent despite sales force strike, says chairman.
